newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher, secondaries rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher, secondaries rebound.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur blue chips continued tracking into new high ground for 1996, while secondary stocks staged a technical rebound after several weak sessions. The Composite Index rose 9.11 to 1,234.73.
Banking stocks, invigorated by news of a 2.16 billion ringgit deal between stockbroker Rashid Hussain and Maybank for Rashid's purchase of 75 percent of Kwong Yik Bank, were a feature, dealers said.
"It was very heavy volume because of the banking story," said Dominic Armstrong, head of research at Pesaka Jardine Fleming.
Banks which gained included United Merchant Group, MIDF and Public Bank. Banking and finance firm Suria Capital, which just debuted on Monday, was the most active issue, up 14 cents to 2.35 ringgit.
"The Second Board rebounded," said an institutional dealer with a foreign house. "To some people, it's bargain-hunting time." The Second Board index jumped 25.75 points or 4.36 percent to 616.76.
Newly-listed steel products maker Ann Joo closed at 5.05 ringgit versus an issue price of 2.00 ringgit.
Volume topped 314 million shares, with advancers ahead of decliners by 342 to 288.
